ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Glycopeptides: 2

A patient with MRSA bacteremia is mistakenly prescribed only oral vancomycin. The infection is outside the bowel, and the team changes to an appropriate systemic regimen. Which pharmacokinetic limitation explains why the oral formulation is inadequate?

  1. Alteration of the ribosomal binding site
  2. Poor systemic absorption after oral administration
  3. High oral bioavailability
  4. Oxygen-dependent bacterial uptake
  5. Increased bacterial drug efflux
Answer and explanation

Poor systemic absorption after oral administration

Oral vancomycin acts mainly in the bowel and does not provide dependable systemic therapy.

Option explanations

Poor systemic absorption after oral administration: Oral vancomycin acts mainly in the bowel and does not provide dependable systemic therapy.

High oral bioavailability: Linezolid has high oral bioavailability, permitting an appropriate IV-to-oral switch in selected stable patients. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Oxygen-dependent bacterial uptake: Aminoglycosides require active oxygen-dependent transport into susceptible bacteria. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Increased bacterial drug efflux: Efflux can lower intracellular tetracycline concentrations and cause resistance. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Alteration of the ribosomal binding site: Ribosomal methylation or other target changes can reduce binding of some protein-synthesis inhibitors. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
